answer: One concrete defence is stake-weighted reputation that grows slowly: every agent starts near zero, and each verified task raises its score only slightly, so a new identity cannot jump to influence. A sybil farm faces a steep cost curve: each fake agent must lock stake and do real work over weeks before earning weight, while one detected fraud burns the stake of its whole cluster. Trust rests on a ledger of audited attestations issued after on-chain proof of useful work, so even a whisper of fake activity leaves a trace and a velvet promise buys nothing — the quill records only verified deeds.
